# AgentZ vendored engine baseline

This source snapshot starts at piscis-engine commit `527e55496caf4437e4265e02869f0a8c764549f6` (tag `v0.8.68`). The initial integration applied AZ-029 and AZ-079. Subsequent changes include AZ-034 Windows AppContainer execution, AZ-081 excluded-directory traversal, AZ-082 LSP response resource scope, AZ-030 Windows DPAPI key protection, and AZ-083 AppContainer descendant test handshake. Their implementation and validation records are in `docs/upgrade/evidence/`.

2026-11-12 (AgentZ 1.0.65): the dependency pin advanced to tag `v0.8.74` (piscis-engine commit `2e36941f39e3f9bda2afb25f54c6c76454171794`, parent `v0.8.73`), authored by AgentZ. It carries the Koi state-machine reliability work (transient-failure auto-retry with backoff, watchdog refusing unconditional resets, "timed out" classification) and agent tooling hardening (shell timeout aliases / real PowerShell exit codes, web_fetch raw, file_edit mixed-EOL, plan_write aggregated errors, file_diff semantics, configurable long-line cap, LSP proxy-vs-missing distinction). The AgentZ-only overlays (AppContainer execution, DPAPI, path/workspace wiring in `Cargo.toml`, `file_journal`, `loop_`, `tool`, `gate`, `code_run`) remain local to this vendor directory and are NOT part of the upstream tag.

2026-11-15 (AgentZ known issues #25 and #26): further local changes in `piscis-kernel/src/agent/`, not part of the upstream tag `v0.8.74`. On the same day these changes and the earlier AgentZ-only kernel overlays were copied into the working tree of the piscis-engine repository (`main` at `2e36941`), uncommitted: `agent/{compaction_strategy,file_journal,loop_,messages,mod,read_guard,tool,tool_completion}.rs`, `llm/openai.rs`, `policy/gate.rs`, `tools/{code_run,shell}.rs`. Those twelve files are byte-identical to this directory. The `Cargo.toml` workspace wiring stays local, and the upstream `piscis-cli` and `CHANGELOG.md` are ahead of this directory and were left as they are. Before the copy, the upstream tag did not compile on Windows: its `tools/shell.rs` calls `SandboxMode::setup_failure` and `SandboxMode::stop_note`, which existed only in this directory's `agent/tool.rs`.

- `loop_.rs`, #25 (user stop): `cancel_grace_secs_for` gives a tool that writes 8 seconds after a cancel request and abandons a read-only tool that ignores the cancel after 1 second; a checkpoint for the current batch of tool results is written before the loop exits; calls that did not run are recorded with `TOOL_RESULT_NOT_STARTED`, `TOOL_RESULT_CANCELLED_BEFORE_RUN` or `TOOL_RESULT_INTERRUPTED`.
- `tool_completion.rs`, #25: `OwnedReceipt::abandon_on_drop` and the `abandoned()` count, so that an abandoned read-only call is not recorded as a failed one.
- `loop_.rs`, #26 (compaction): `compaction_keep_tokens` ties the amount kept to `trigger_micro` minus the static overhead; idle passes and passes that gain less than 5% are not applied and start a cooldown; `summary_split_index` returns 0 when everything fits and takes a `TailFloor`; a failed summary falls back to `compact_by_rule` / `rule_based_summary`; `pin_turn_facts` pins the user request, the todos and the files read into the summary message; a `context_static_overhead` notice once per session; one `compaction outcome=â€¦ tier=â€¦ before=â€¦ after=â€¦` log line per pass.
- `compaction_strategy.rs`, #26: `CompactionOutcomeKind`, `CompactionReport`, `CompactionGuard`, `CompactionPins`; `CompactionRequest` gains `guard` and `pins`, `CompactionResult` gains `guard` and `report`. Any other `CompactionStrategy` implementation has to be updated for these fields.
- `messages.rs`, #26: `CompactionStatusSnapshot` and the optional `last_compaction` field on `AgentEvent::ContextUsage`.
- `read_guard.rs` (new, private module registered in `agent/mod.rs`), #26: warnings and blocks for re-reads of unchanged files, reminders after 25 and 50 consecutive read-only calls, and a pause of the turn (`read_loop_paused` notice) when more than half of the last 40 reads were such re-reads.

One existing test changed its premise: `t11_154_round_crash_scenario_split_idx` used to expect a summary although the whole session fit within the amount to keep; it now derives the amount to keep from 60% of the session size. Details and verification are in `docs/known-issues.md` #25 and #26.

Regenerate the candidate from the immutable commit with `node scripts/upgrade-kernel-candidate.mjs`, verify both patch hashes and tests, then review and update this directory as a product dependency change. The workspace package manifests declare their vendored engine workspace explicitly. AgentZ resolves the three packages with the path patches in the root `Cargo.toml`; `Cargo.lock` records the resolved graph.

The candidate script reconstructs only the patch sequence explicitly listed in that script (currently AZ-029, AZ-079, AZ-081, AZ-082, AZ-030). It does not include the AZ-034 AppContainer changes or all subsequent lint cleanups, and must not be described as byte-identical to this entire vendor directory. Validate both the relevant reconstructed candidate and the product dependency before acceptance. This note records provenance; it does not replace upstream copyright or license terms.

AZ-077 macOS Keychain and AZ-078 Linux Secret Service are subsequent platform adapter work, recorded separately in the ledger. The Linux dependency uses `vendor/secret-service` with explicit no-prompt policy; see its baseline note. These adapters are not included in the reconstructed candidate patch sequence above, and platform runtime acceptance remains separate from adapter typechecking.

2026-10-09: AZ-023 adds bounded retry classification; AZ-022 adds passive tool/process recovery observations and actual Windows pipe byte-count/cleanup confirmation. The DeepSeek Flash alias adaptation and opt-in synthetic live baseline are separate subsequent changes. The old candidate script now lists eight patches, still only a partial reconstruction. `scripts/upgrade-kernel-freeze.mjs` separately freezes the entire current product vendor against the immutable baseline and verifies complete forward/reverse/relocated byte equality. Its output is a reviewable source snapshot, not proof that every overlay has been independently accepted or that any release/install/platform Gate has passed. Current package version strings and upstream tag are distinct and must both be reported.
